paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: in this whole courtroom, the only one who is truly in charge is the one standing there bound. Everybody is shouting, scrambling and covering themselves. Pilate says he has authority to release Jesus and authority to crucify Him, and Jesus answers, "You would have no authority over Me if it were not given to you from above." (John 19:11) Pilate thinks he's running the room, but he's like a man waving his arms at an oven timer. The timer doesn't care!

Now look at what each person does with the truth. Pilate says three times, "I find no basis for a charge against Him," and then he hands Jesus over anyway. (John 19:6) The chief priests say, "We have no king but Caesar," and the King of the Jews is standing right in front of them. (John 19:15) Jesus said, "Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to My voice." (John 18:37) I think that's the question this passage puts to us. Knowing the truth is one thing, and listening to Jesus is another.

And here's why it matters to you. Jesus' kingdom is "not of this world," so He never needed to win a fight or beat a crowd. (John 18:36) The writer even tells us that what was happening fulfilled what Jesus had said about the kind of death He was going to die. (John 18:32) Nothing in that courtroom caught Him off guard, and I'm telling you, that is a King worth listening to. So when the crowd is loud and the pressure is on, baker, listen to His voice. The story isn't over!
